title: Vitamin D Promotes Neuronal Survival via Nrf2 Upregulation in D-Galactose-Induced Mice: An In-Vivo and In-Silico Study.
authors: Shah, Fawad Ali; Zakria, Muhammad; Bin Dayel, Faten F; Rehman, Najeeb Ur; Jahan, Sarwat; Ikram, Muhammad
journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该研究主要探讨维生素D通过Nrf2通路在D-半乳糖诱导小鼠中的神经保护作用，分子对接仅涉及维生素D与Nrf2蛋白（非DNA）结合，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: Gradual loss of the homeostatic balance owing to deregulation of endogenous antioxidant defense pathways, such as nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), contributes, at least in part, to the characteristic oxidative stress, neuronal loss, and cognitive decline associated with aging. Here, we adopted an integrated approach using behavioral, biochemical, histological, molecular, and in silico methods, exploring the neuroprotective efficacy of vitamin D against D-galactose-induced oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. Chronic D-galactose administration (150 mg/kg, s.c) led to profound deficits in spatial learning, working memory, and recognition memory, besides increased oxidative stress, reduced antioxidant enzyme activity, suppression of Nrf2 and heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) expression, and frank hippocampal neurodegeneration, as revealed by nissl staining. Vitamin D treatment (5 microg/kg i.p) significantly improved such deficits by restoring cognitive performance, reducing ROS and lipid peroxidation, enhancing endogenous antioxidant activities such as superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), reduced glutathione (GSH) and glutathione peroxidase (GPx), and upregulating Nrf2 and HO-1 expression comparable to positive control, dimethyl fumarate (DMF). Co-administration of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), an antagonist for Nrf2, abrogated these protective effects, confirming the pathway specificity. Molecular docking studies have shown a strong binding affinity of Vitamin D to the regulatory domain of Nrf2, supporting a direct stabilizing interaction that may facilitate the activation of Nrf2. Nissl quantification has further demonstrated substantial preservation of neuronal integrity in hippocampal CA1, CA3, and DG regions following the treatment with vitamin D. Altogether, findings from this study show that vitamin D confers robust neuroprotection through Nrf2-dependent antioxidant mechanisms and mitigates aging-related neurodegeneration induced by D-galactose. The results highlighted vitamin D as a readily accessible therapeutic candidate for mitigating oxidative stress-driven cognitive decline.
abstract_zh: 内源性抗氧化防御通路（如核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2））的失调导致稳态平衡逐渐丧失，至少部分地促成了与衰老相关的特征性氧化应激、神经元丢失和认知衰退。在此，我们采用了一种整合方法，结合行为学、生物化学、组织学、分子和计算机模拟手段，探讨维生素D对D-半乳糖诱导的氧化应激、神经炎症和神经变性的神经保护功效。慢性D-半乳糖给药（150 mg/kg，皮下注射）导致空间学习、工作记忆和识别记忆的严重缺陷，此外还增加了氧化应激、降低了抗氧化酶活性、抑制了Nrf2和血红素加氧酶-1（HO-1）的表达，并通过尼氏染色揭示了明显的海马神经变性。维生素D治疗（5微克/kg，腹腔注射）显著改善了这些缺陷，表现为恢复认知表现、减少活性氧（ROS）和脂质过氧化、增强内源性抗氧化活性（如超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）、过氧化氢酶（CAT）、还原型谷胱甘肽（GSH）和谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶（GPx）），并上调Nrf2和HO-1表达，与阳性对照富马酸二甲酯（DMF）相当。联合给予全反式维甲酸（ATRA）（一种Nrf2拮抗剂）消除了这些保护效应，证实了通路特异性。分子对接研究表明，维生素D与Nrf2的调控域具有强结合亲和力，支持可能促进Nrf2激活的直接稳定相互作用。尼氏定量进一步显示，维生素D治疗后，海马CA1、CA3和DG区域的神经元完整性得到显著保留。总体而言，本研究结果表明，维生素D通过Nrf2依赖性抗氧化机制赋予强大的神经保护作用，并减轻D-半乳糖诱导的衰老相关神经变性。结果突显了维生素D作为缓解氧化应激驱动的认知衰退的易获取治疗候选药物。
